title: Personal Training Packages: how a package is priced and dated at purchase
content:
## Scope
This document covers the Personal Training Packages product line and states the basis on which a package is priced at purchase and on which its expiration date is set.

## Rule
At purchase, the package is priced at the tier's own listed price, reduced by the multi-package discount rate if the member already holds another open package, and reduced by the corporate wellness discount rate if the member holds an active corporate wellness enrollment -- taking whichever single one of those two discounts is higher rather than applying both together. The package's expiration date is set to the purchase date plus the tier's own expiration window, counted in calendar days.

~~The package grants the tier's own listed number of sessions at purchase (or unlimited use, subject to the tier's weekly fair-use cap, when the tier's listed session count denotes unlimited use).~~ This clause is no longer in force for how many sessions are actually credited to the package once activated; the current basis for the number of sessions credited at activation is stated in the package-activation documents for this product.

## Points of judgement
Only one of the multi-package discount and the corporate wellness discount is ever applied to the listed price, never both together: where a member qualifies for both because they already hold another open package and hold an active corporate wellness enrollment, the higher of the two discount rates is the one applied, and the lower one is disregarded rather than added on top. Where a member qualifies for neither, the package is priced at the tier's own listed price with no discount. The expiration date calculation always starts from the purchase date itself and runs forward by the tier's own expiration window in full calendar days, with no partial-day rounding.
